Date: 2021-08-19 WHAT IS CLAIMED IS:
1. A pressure sensing mat comprising:
a first portion including a first conductive layer contacting a first non-conductive layer, wherein the first conductive layer is continuous except for a first plurality of discontinuities defining a first plurality of conductive strips oriented in a first direction;
a second portion including a second conductive layer layered to a second non- conductive layer, wherein the second conductive layer is continuous except for a second plurality of discontinuities defining a second plurality of conductive strips oriented in a second direction; and
an insulative layer disposed between the first portion and the second portion, wherein the first plurality of conductive strips and the second plurality of conductive strips form a conductive strip matrix having a plurality of capacitors wherein each capacitors of the plurality of capacitors are configured to provide a capacitance indicative of a pressure applied at each capacitor of the plurality of capacitors.
2. The pressure sensing mat of claim 1, wherein the first portion includes a first end and a second end, wherein each conductive strip of the first plurality of conductive strips are formed as columns including a first column and a second column, wherein the first column has a first width and is spaced apart from the first end by a first distance and the second column has a second width greater than the first width and is spaced apart from the first end by a second distance, greater than the first distance.
3. The pressure sensing mat of claim 2, wherein a number of columns are disposed between the first column and the second column, wherein a width of each of the columns differs between the first and second columns.
4. The pressure sensing mat of claim 3, wherein the width of each of the columns disposed between the first and second columns monotonically increases from the first end to the second end.
5. The pressure sensing mat of claim 2, wherein when the pressure sensing mat is used to detect a pressure of an individual, the first portion is arranged to face towards the individual.
6. The pressure sensing mat of claim 5, wherein when the pressure sensing mat is used to detect pressure of the individual, the second end of the mat is configured to be arranged beneath a head of the individual.
7. The pressure sensing mat of claim 1, wherein the second direction is substantially orthogonal to the first direction.
8. The pressure sensing mat of claim 1, wherein the first non-conductive layer is continuous except for a third plurality of discontinuities, wherein the third plurality of discontinuities correspond to the first plurality of discontinuities.
9. The pressure sensing mat of claim 8, wherein the first conductive layer is disposed between the first non-conductive layer and the insulative layer.
10. The pressure sensing mat of claim 8, wherein the second non-conductive layer is continuous except for a fourth plurality of discontinuities, wherein the fourth plurality of discontinuities correspond to the third plurality of discontinuities.
11. The pressure sensing mat of claim 10, wherein the second conductive layer is disposed between the second non-conductive layer and the insulative layer.
12. A pressure sensing mat comprising:
a first portion including a first conductive layer sandwiched between a first non- conductive layer and a second non-conductive layer, wherein the first non-conductive layer and the first conductive layer define a first set of channels at least partially enclosing a first conductive strip extending in a first direction;
a second portion including a second conductive layer sandwiched between a third non-conductive layer and a fourth non-conductive layer, wherein the third non-conductive layer and the second conductive layer define a second set of channels at least partially enclosing a second conductive strip extending in a second direction; and
an insulative layer disposed between the first portion and the second portion, wherein the first conductive strip and the second conductive strip form a capacitor configured to provide a capacitance indicative of a pressure applied to the capacitor.
13. The pressure sensing mat of claim 12, wherein the first set of channels at least partially enclose a third conductive strip and the second set of channels at least partially enclose a fourth conductive strip, wherein the third conductive strip and the fourth conductive strip form a second capacitor configured to provide a capacitance indicative of a pressure applied to the second capacitor, wherein the first portion includes a first set of conductive leads .
14. The pressure sensing mat of claim 13, wherein the first portion includes a second set of conductive leads, wherein the first conductive strip is disposed in a left region of the first portion and the third conductive strip is disposed in a right region of the first portion.
15. The pressure sensing mat of claim 14, wherein the first set of conductive leads are disposed on a first side of the first portion and at least a portion of the second set of conductive leads are disposed on a second side of the first portion, wherein the second side opposes the first side.
16. The pressure sensing mat of claim 15, wherein the first set of conductive leads are formed by a third set of channels extending substantially in the second direction and defined by the first non-conductive layer and the first conductive layer.
17. The pressure sensing mat of claim 16, wherein the first set of conductive leads are formed by a fourth set of channels extending in the first direction and defined by the first non- conductive layer and the first conductive layer.
18. The pressure sensing mat of claim 17, wherein the first set of conductive leads are disposed in a connection region of the pressure sensing mat including a peripheral area and a medial area, wherein the first set of conductive leads includes a first conductive lead and a second conductive lead, wherein the first conductive lead has a first length and is disposed in the peripheral area and the second conductive lead has a second length, greater than the first length and is disposed in the medial area.
19. The pressure sensing mat of claim 18, wherein the first set of conductive leads include a number of conductive leads disposed between the first conductive lead and the second conductive lead, wherein a length of the each of the conductive leads disposed between the first conductive lead and the second conductive lead monotonically decreases from the peripheral area to the medial area.
20. The pressure sensing mat of claim 19, wherein the second set of conductive leads includes a first segment, a second segment, and a third segment, wherein the first segment is disposed on the second side of the first portion, the second segment extends in the first direction from the first set of signal detecting leads, and the third segment extends from the second segment.
21. The pressure sensing mat of claim 20, wherein the first segment is substantially orthogonal to the second segment.
22. The pressure sensing mat of claim 20, wherein at least one of the conductive leads of the first set of conductive leads has a first width and the first conductive strip has a second width greater than the first width.
23. The pressure sensing mat of claim 12, wherein the first conductive layer has a first surface area, the first non-conductive layer has a second surface area, and the second non- conductive layer has a third surface area, wherein the first surface area is greater than the second and third surface areas.
24. The pressure sensing mat of claim 12, wherein the first portion has a first thickness wherein the first set of channels has a first depth that is less than the first thickness.
25. The pressure sensing mat of claim 12, wherein the first and second non- conductive layers are each laminated to the conductive layer.
26. The pressure sensing mat of claim 12, wherein the first conductive layer is formed of copper.
27. The pressure sensing mat of claim 26, wherein the first conductive layer has a surface resistivity of at least 0.10 ohms.
28. A method of making a pressure sensing mat, the method comprising:
providing a first laminated sheet including a first non-conductive layer, a second non- conductive layer, and a first conductive layer sandwiched therebetween;
providing a second laminated sheet including a third non-conductive layer, a fourth non-conductive layer, and a second conductive layer sandwiched therebetween;
removing portions of the first laminated sheet to define a first plurality of channels to form a first plurality of conductive strips extending in a first direction;
removing portions of the second laminated sheet to define a second plurality of channels to form a second plurality of conductive strips extending in a second direction;
attaching the first laminated layer to a first side of an insulative layer; and
attaching the second laminated layer to a second side of the insulative layer.
29. The method of claim 28, wherein the removing steps each include etching the first and second laminated layers.
30. The method of claim 28, wherein the removing steps each include applying a laser to melt the portions of the first and second laminated layers. 23 24 25 26 27
